_readme: An entry here is a REASONED exemption, never a silenced finding (D786: fix
what the scanners find; an exemption must be reasoned, not skipped). Each
one states WHY the ungated emission does not produce the ~3px browser
default, so the next reader can re-check the reason rather than trust the
row. If the stated reason stops being true, delete the entry — the gate is
Add an entry ONLY when gating the emission would make the render WORSE.

entries.reason: sgs/button never reaches the browser's UA default: its own style.css:45 declares a real `border-width: 2px` on the element. Gating the style here would be a REGRESSION, not a fix — a button set to `dashed` with no explicit width would lose the dashed style while keeping the stylesheet's 2px, rendering 2px SOLID instead of 2px dashed. The defect this gate exists to catch (a style falling through to `medium`) cannot occur on this block.
entries.recheck: If button/style.css ever stops declaring border-width, this exemption is void and the emission must be gated. Verify with: grep -n 'border-width' plugins/sgs-blocks/src/blocks/button/style.css
entries.authority: G5 branch analysis, independently re-verified against button/style.css:45
